name: Apple Xcode Cloud

modes.label: Xcode Cloud compute hours (Xcode build/test only)

sizes.name: Xcode Cloud compute hour (Apple-managed, spec not published)

modes.note: Hour price = marginal rate of the 250 h / 1,000 h / 10,000 h subscriptions ($99.99/250, $399.99/1,000, $3,999.99/10,000 = ~$0.40/h). Hour packs are encoded as plans with included_usd = hours x $0.40. A compute hour is summed task time ("running 5 tests of 12 minutes each equals one compute hour").

plans.name: Included with Apple Developer Program (25 h/month)
plans.note: Requires Apple Developer Program membership ($99/yr). 25 compute hours/month; unused hours don't roll over; no overage - builds beyond the quota need a paid subscription.

caveats: Xcode build/test workflows only: Xcode Cloud runs Xcode actions (build, test, analyze, archive) for Apple-platform apps. Shell runs only as the three custom build-script hooks (ci_post_clone.sh, ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh, ci_post_xcodebuild.sh) inside a workflow, without sudo ("You can't obtain administrator privileges by using sudo"), and files they create are deleted. No SSH, no interactive shell, no GUI/desktop automation: not usable as an agent sandbox or macOS desktop.
Subscriptions are fixed hour packs with no published overage; beyond the pack you must upgrade. included_usd at $0.40/h approximates that; the 100 h pack is really $0.50/h.
Billing granularity not published (granularity_s null); ephemeral build environments are destroyed after each build.
Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year = $8.25/month) is required and is included in every plan fee here.

Upgrading a subscription starts a new billing period immediately and resets the quota to 0 (new plan's hours replace, not add to, the remainder); downgrades take effect next period; cancel -> back to 25 h.
Subscriptions are priced in USD or in local currency where available (local prices shown only in the Apple Developer app; localized web pages jp/cn list the same US$ prices).
Hidden infrastructure-validation builds may run duplicate builds/custom scripts (opt-out in App Store Connect); Apple says they don't consume your build minutes.

fleet.verification: Apple Developer Program membership; Account Holder manages subscriptions.
fleet.tiers: Subscriptions purchase monthly compute hours (25 included, higher paid tiers); not a published concurrent-build fleet allocation.
fleet.notes: No universal new-account concurrent build/VM quota or increase-review SLA found. Parallel build/test operations consume hours; simulator count and build hours must not be equated to machine concurrency.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Xcode Cloud performs each action separately in a temporary build environment. As a result, an action’s artifacts might not be available to other actions.
snapshot_auto.note: Build environments are temporary and discarded. Only an automatic build cache exists ('Xcode Cloud stores each build’s derived data and other cached information for reuse', workflow reference; clean builds can be forced), which is not machine state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Xcode Cloud performs each action separately in a temporary build environment.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint concept in docs or the App Store Connect API (workflows, builds, artifacts only). Environment = chosen macOS + Xcode version, not a custom image.

harness_api.quote: Xcode Cloud supports running custom shell scripts, referred to as custom build scripts.
harness_api.note: CI service: runs Xcode build/test/analyze/archive actions plus three hook scripts (ci_post_clone.sh, ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh, ci_post_xcodebuild.sh). No agent harness, no interactive exec API.

ingress_rules.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
ingress_rules.note: Not applicable in practice: no inbound access to build machines at all (no SSH, no exposed ports, no preview URLs), so there are no ingress rules to configure.

guest_firewall.quote: You can’t obtain administrator privileges by using sudo in your custom build scripts.
guest_firewall.note: No root, so pf/firewall rules cannot be set inside the macOS build VM.

secret_proxy.quote: If you mark a custom environment variable to be a secret, Xcode Cloud replaces its value with asterisks (**********) in build logs.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are custom environment variables (per workflow or shared across workflows) exposed to build scripts; only redacted in logs. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Files you create with a custom build script aren’t available to other custom build scripts, and Xcode Cloud deletes any files a custom build script creates.
volume_attach.note: No volume product; storage is the temporary build environment plus downloadable build artifacts and Apple's internal derived-data cache.

volume_shared.quote: As a result, an action’s artifacts might not be available to other actions.
volume_shared.note: Parallel actions do not share a filesystem.

isolation.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
isolation.note: Apple-managed macOS build environment per action; no root/sudo, no SSH, spec not published (consistent with the card's existing apple-vm classification for a macOS CI runner).

image_oci.quote: To configure a workflow's temporary build environment, navigate to the workflow's Environment section, and choose from available Xcode and macOS versions.
image_oci.note: Only a picklist of Apple-provided Xcode/macOS version combinations; no custom Docker/OCI image or custom base-image upload capability exists.

anti_bot.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a build/test/archive CI service, not a browser/scraping product)

captcha_solving.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI build/test runner, no browser automation)

wake_on_request.quote: When you create a new workflow, Xcode suggests the Branch Changes condition that starts a new build for every change to your Git repository's default branch.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Xcode Cloud spins up a fresh temporary build environment per triggered build (git push, PR, tag, schedule, or manual/API start) rather than waking an existing stopped/sleeping machine on an inbound request.

live_resize.quote: Xcode Cloud... an Apple-managed continuous integration and delivery service.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Build machine spec is fixed and Apple-managed per build; there is no running machine to resize (each action gets its own temporary environment, then it is discarded).

own_agent_api.quote: use the App Store Connect API to manage workflows, start builds, and access Xcode Cloud data.
own_agent_api.note: The only first-party API (App Store Connect API) manages CI workflows/builds/artifacts; there is no browser/computer-use/research task agent to drive.

mcp_server.quote: use the App Store Connect API to manage workflows, start builds, and access Xcode Cloud data.
mcp_server.note: No MCP server for Xcode Cloud found in Apple's developer documentation; only the REST-based App Store Connect API is offered.

lang_python.quote: The temporary build environment that Xcode Cloud uses includes tools that are part of macOS and Xcode — for example, Python

lang_node.quote: The temporary build environment Xcode Cloud uses to perform a build doesn't include third-party tools or dependencies. However, it includes Homebrew, an open source package manager you can use to install additional software.
lang_node.note: Docs explicitly call out Python and pre-installed CocoaPods/Homebrew as included tools but never mention Node.js/npm as preinstalled; Node would have to be installed via a custom build script with Homebrew, so it is not available out of the box.

egress_allowlist.quote: Xcode Cloud builds your project using temporary build environments that use an HTTP proxy and makes the standard http_proxy and https_proxy environment variables available.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: no provider-side outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is documented for Xcode Cloud build environments.

egress_http_rules.quote: Xcode Cloud builds your project using temporary build environments that use an HTTP proxy...
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no method/path-level egress rule configuration is documented; the HTTP proxy exists for routing, not for customer-configured egress policy.

static_egress_ip.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed/static outbound IP is documented or offered for build environments; not applicable to this CI product.

soc2.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
soc2.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Apple does not publish a SOC 2 report or attestation for Xcode Cloud on its developer/pricing/docs pages; it targets individual/team developers under the Apple Developer Program, not enterprise compliance buyers.

hipaa.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No HIPAA-eligibility or BAA offering is documented for Xcode Cloud; it is a build/test CI runner, not a data-processing service marketed for regulated health data.

sso.quote: Xcode Cloud is available to Apple Developer Program members.
sso.note: not offered: access is through Apple ID / Apple Developer Program membership and App Store Connect team roles; no customer-configurable SAML/OIDC SSO integration is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and App Store Connect, designed expressly for Apple developers.
eu_data_residency.note: not offered: no region/data-residency selection is documented for where Xcode Cloud build environments or data run; Apple manages infrastructure location itself.

persistent_disk.quote: Source code is only accessed for builds and the ephemeral build environments are destroyed when your build completes.
persistent_disk.note: Also: 'Xcode Cloud deletes any files a custom build script creates' (writing-custom-build-scripts). Every build gets a fresh, temporary environment; nothing persists across builds or actions.

snapshot.quote: the ephemeral build environments are destroyed when your build completes.
snapshot.note: No snapshot/checkpoint concept anywhere in the Xcode Cloud docs or App Store Connect API; only build artifacts and a derived-data cache are kept.

pause_resume.quote: Xcode Cloud automatically cancels an in-progress build if a workflow queues a new build for the same workflow.
pause_resume.note: The only lifecycle controls documented are start/cancel of a build; there is no pause/resume of a build environment (which is destroyed on completion anyway).

fork.quote: Xcode Cloud performs each action separately in a temporary build environment.
fork.note: There is no machine/VM object exposed to the user at all (only workflows/builds/actions), so there is nothing to clone.

fork_running.quote: Xcode Cloud performs each action separately in a temporary build environment.
fork_running.note: No concept of a running machine that could be cloned; each action's environment is ephemeral and per-action.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: the ephemeral build environments are destroyed when your build completes.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork feature exists at all, so a memory-preserving fork does not either.

docker_inside.quote: You can’t obtain administrator privileges by using sudo in your custom build scripts.
docker_inside.note: Custom build scripts (the only shell access offered) run without sudo/root, which rules out running a Docker daemon inside the build environment.

nested_virt.quote: You can’t obtain administrator privileges by using sudo in your custom build scripts.
nested_virt.note: No root/admin access and no documented virtualization framework exposure inside the temporary macOS build environment.

root.quote: You can’t obtain administrator privileges by using sudo in your custom build scripts.
root.note: Explicit statement that sudo/admin privileges are unavailable.

ssh.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
ssh.note: Xcode Cloud is a CI/CD build-action product; the only way to run code in the environment is the three custom-build-script hooks. No SSH or interactive-shell access is documented anywhere; outside what the product offers.

desktop.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and designed expressly for Apple developers.
desktop.note: Xcode Cloud only runs Xcode build/test/analyze/archive actions in an ephemeral headless environment; no GUI/VNC/streamed desktop is offered — outside what the product is.

browser.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and designed expressly for Apple developers.
browser.note: A CI/CD build-action service for Xcode projects has no managed/embedded browser; outside what the product is.

computer_use.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and designed expressly for Apple developers.
computer_use.note: No screenshot/click driving API exists; the environment isn't interactive at all (build actions + 3 script hooks only).

custom_image.quote: To configure a workflow’s temporary build environment, navigate to the workflow’s Environment section, and choose from available Xcode and macOS versions.
custom_image.note: You pick from Apple's predefined Xcode/macOS version combinations; there is no way to supply your own base image.

volumes.quote: Files you create with a custom build script aren’t available to other custom build scripts, and Xcode Cloud deletes any files a custom build script creates.
volumes.note: No persistent-volume product exists; even files within a single build don't reliably persist across script/action boundaries.

inbound_https.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
inbound_https.note: Build environments are private/isolated CI runners with no exposed ports or public URLs; there is nothing to route inbound HTTPS to.

public_ipv4.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
public_ipv4.note: No networking/IP configuration is exposed to users of the CI build service; outside what the product offers.

agent_harnesses.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and designed expressly for Apple developers.
agent_harnesses.note: Xcode Cloud runs Xcode build/test/archive actions and shell build-script hooks; no coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) are offered or preinstalled.

gpu.quote: Xcode Cloud allocates resources in parallel to quickly complete the testing job while you and your Mac keep coding.
gpu.note: Xcode Cloud only advertises macOS build/test compute hours (Apple-managed, spec not published); no GPU compute product is offered.

windows.quote: Xcode Cloud is a continuous integration and delivery service built into Xcode and designed expressly for Apple developers.
windows.note: Xcode Cloud builds Apple-platform (iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS) apps on Apple's macOS build machines only; no Windows machines are offered.

self_host.quote: As builds happen in the cloud, Xcode shows live status indicators and lets you filter by the build tasks you want to monitor.
self_host.note: Xcode Cloud is a fully Apple-hosted service tied to App Store Connect / Apple Developer Program; there is no self-hosted deployment option.

byoc.quote: As builds happen in the cloud, Xcode shows live status indicators and lets you filter by the build tasks you want to monitor.
byoc.note: No option to deploy the service into a customer-owned cloud account; it runs entirely on Apple's own infrastructure.

open_source.quote: Xcode Cloud requires Apple Developer Program membership.
open_source.note: Xcode Cloud is a closed, proprietary Apple service (paid subscription tiers, membership-gated); no OSI-licensed core product exists.

private_network.quote: Xcode Cloud clones your repository in a private, isolated, and temporary build environment.
private_network.note: "Private, isolated" describes per-build sandboxing, not a user-configurable private network; no VPC/private-networking feature is documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: Xcode Cloud builds your project using temporary build environments that use an HTTP proxy and makes the standard HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables available.
egress_ip_type.note: All outbound network traffic from a build is routed through Apple's own HTTP proxy in the temporary build environment, i.e. Apple-managed datacenter infrastructure, not a residential/mobile IP pool. Apple does not publish specific outbound IP addresses/ranges or a static-egress-IP feature (consistent with static_egress_ip=false already on this card), so this is Apple's own (non-static) datacenter egress rather than a customer-visible IP product.

usage_api.quote: Billing granularity not published; usage is subscription-based monthly hour quotas (25/100/250/1,000/10,000 hours) visible only through App Store Connect dashboard, not via REST API or machine-readable endpoint.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; App Store Connect API can retrieve build metadata but not billable usage metrics. Usage is viewed only in the UI dashboard.
